findings.function: assertionError() and the 8 other Panic constants (arithmeticError, divisionError, enumConversionError, encodeStorageError, popError, indexOOBError, memOverflowError, zeroVarError)
findings.source: forge-std StdError.sol: bytes public constant assertionError = abi.encodeWithSignature("Panic(uint256)", 0x01);
findings.issue: The 36-byte constant is printed as two 32-byte words, so the Panic code 1 appears as 1 << 224 (0x1000...0 with 57 digits) instead of a 4-byte selector followed by the word 1.
findings.rule: Print a constant byte string of length n by its own layout: when n = 4 + 32k, as Bytes(4, selector) followed by k words (0x4e487b71, 1).

notes: Library of constant getters, no loops and no storage. The 9 getters return the right Panic payloads (codes 0x01, 0x11, 0x12, 0x21, 0x22, 0x31, 0x32, 0x41, 0x51); 'payable' reflects the absence of a callvalue check in this library bytecode. Only assertionError is named by the signature database.
summary: Correct; the only issue is the word-wise printing of the 36-byte Panic payloads.
